checkSelf.title: Refrigerator Self-check
checkSelf.titleInfoDesc:
1. The self-check result is for reference only. An abnormal result does not necessarily mean the refrigerator has a fault.

2. The purpose of refrigerator self-check is to help you troubleshoot or request service in time when you suspect there may be a problem.
checkSelf.statusNormal: Your refrigerator is operating normally. Please use it with confidence.
checkSelf.statusNeedCheck: Your refrigerator may need inspection. If cooling is normal, please ignore this result.
checkSelf.tipIntro: The self-check result is for reference only and does not necessarily mean there is a problem. Please check the following:
checkSelf.tipItems:
1. Whether the air outlet in the compartment is blocked by foreign objects;
2. Whether the door has been opened frequently in the last 2 hours, left open for a long time, or hot food has been stored inside.
checkSelf.tipFooter: Any of the above may reduce the cooling performance of the refrigerator. If any applies, remove the blockage and close the door for 2 hours before checking again.

process.description: Note: The detection result only covers the main refrigerator modules and does not represent all possible faults. Please refer to the actual issue during use. The result is for reference only.

solutions.refrigerateBad:
1. Make sure the refrigerator compartment switch is turned on. If Holiday Mode is available, make sure it is turned off.
2. Try lowering the temperature setting and reduce the number of times the door is opened.
3. Avoid putting in overly hot food. For non-built-in models, keep 5-10 cm space from the wall to improve cooling performance.
4. After first power-on or after the door has been open for a long time, wait 2 hours before checking the cooling effect.
solutions.freezeBad:
1. Adjust the position of stored items to avoid blocking the air outlet.
2. After first power-on or after the door has been open for a long time, wait 2 hours before checking the cooling effect.
3. If too much food is placed in at once, it may take 2-6 hours to cool down.
solutions.sideHeat: 1. The sides of the refrigerator dissipate heat during cooling (bottom heat dissipation for built-in series), so the temperature may rise. Please scan the QR code on the appliance and check the required side heat dissipation clearance.
solutions.sideHeat_oversea: 1. The sides of the refrigerator dissipate heat during cooling (bottom heat dissipation for built-in series), so the temperature may rise. Please check the manual and check the required side heat dissipation clearance.
solutions.noiseLoud:
1. First make sure the refrigerator is level. If it is not, scan the QR code on the appliance to view the electronic manual and try to adjust it to a balanced position.
2. Some sounds during operation are normal and unavoidable, such as refrigerant flow, compressor noise, and fan noise. Avoid placing the refrigerator in resting areas. The sound may feel more obvious in a small room or at night, so placing it in the kitchen is recommended.
3. Try closing the door again. If the door is not tightly closed, there may be an alarm sound.
solutions.noiseLoud_oversea:
1. First make sure the refrigerator is level. If it is not, try to adjust it to a balanced position.
2. Some sounds during operation are normal and unavoidable, such as refrigerant flow, compressor noise, and fan noise. Avoid placing the refrigerator in resting areas. The sound may feel more obvious in a small room or at night, so placing it in the kitchen is recommended.
3. Try closing the door again. If the door is not tightly closed, there may be an alarm sound.
solutions.powerNoResponse:
1. Check whether the refrigerator power cord is damaged.
2. Check whether the plug has power and whether the power cord is firmly plugged in.
solutions.buttonNoResponse: 1. Check whether Child Lock is enabled (small lock icon on the display). If yes, press and hold Child Lock for 3 seconds before operating again.
solutions.freezeIce: 1. If the refrigerator door stays open for a long time, moisture in the air can enter the freezer and cause heavy icing. Icing may be more severe in rapid cooling mode. Please confirm whether the door is currently or was previously not fully closed. If the door was left open for a long time, defrost first, close the door, and wait 6 hours before checking again.
solutions.freezeIce_oversea: 1. If the refrigerator door stays open for a long time, moisture in the air can enter the freezer and cause heavy icing. Please confirm whether the door is currently or was previously not fully closed. If the door was left open for a long time, defrost first, close the door, and wait 6 hours before checking again.
solutions.smell:
1. Some new plastic parts may have a normal factory odor, which is harmless and will gradually disappear over time. Before use, open the door for ventilation or wipe the interior once with clean water.
2. Clean the refrigerator, especially stains attached to the inside, and check whether the odor remains after cleaning.
3. Avoid storing strongly smelling food for a long time. You may place orange peel or pomelo peel inside to help remove the odor.
